artifacts.title: DNS zone transfer to LFI/SMB RCE and Python lib hijack root (FriendZone)
artifacts.starting_access: unauthenticated access to DNS, SMB and HTTPS on an Ubuntu 18.04 host
artifacts.outcome: root via Python standard library hijacking in a root cron
transferable_properties: DNS TCP on port 53 means zone transfer is worth trying
SMB share comments leak filesystem paths
LFI plus a writable network share gives RCE
run pspy to confirm root executes a script before modifying files
world-writable Python standard library files in a root cron are an instant root

hypotheses.statement: zone transfer reveals subdomains and SMB leaks credentials

selected_action.intent: attempt a DNS zone transfer and enumerate SMB shares

evidence.summary: dig axfr revealed administrator1/hr/uploads subdomains; SMB general share contained creds.txt

observations: Development SMB share is writable and maps to /etc/Development

hypotheses.statement: uploading a webshell to the writable share and including it via LFI gives RCE

selected_action.intent: upload a PHP webshell via SMB and include it via the pagename LFI

evidence.summary: uploaded shell.php to the Development share and included it via pagename to get RCE as www-data

hypotheses.statement: the database password is reused for the friend system user

selected_action.intent: read mysql_data.conf and try the credentials with su

evidence.summary: used the credentials from mysql_data.conf to su to friend, obtaining the user flag

observations: root runs reporter.py (which imports os) via cron every minute

hypotheses.statement: appending a SUID payload to os.py makes the root cron create a SUID bash

selected_action.intent: append a SUID payload to os.py and wait for the root cron

evidence.summary: appended a chmod +s /bin/bash line to os.py, waited for the cron, and ran /bin/bash -p as root

execution_examples.capability_hint: privilege escalation via Python standard library hijacking in a root cron
execution_examples.purpose: append a SUID payload to a world-writable Python module imported by a root cron

prerequisites.statement: os.py is world-writable and the root cron imports os via reporter.py
